document_info.title: ApeForest Species Cards — Reference Sources & Knowledge Basis
document_info.project: Tekoá Kuaray Rese Reforestation, Osório, Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil
document_info.purpose: Documents the primary sources, databases and knowledge frameworks used to populate species data and justify ecological scores for all 33 native Atlantic Forest / RS Pampa species in the Tekoá Kuaray Rese planting.
document_info.transparency_note: ApeForest scores are derived from a combination of peer-reviewed botanical literature, Brazilian government flora databases, iNaturalist observation records, and established Atlantic Forest restoration frameworks. Where specific measurements are unavailable for a species, scores are extrapolated from related taxa and general Atlantic Forest successional ecology. All extrapolations are flagged per species below.
document_info.important_disclaimer: CO₂ absorption figures are estimates based on published allometric equations and wood density data. They are indicative values for educational and communication purposes, not certified carbon credits. Site-specific measurements from Tekoá Kuaray Rese monitoring will supersede these estimates as field data is collected.

global_reference_databases.name: Flora e Funga do Brasil
global_reference_databases.description: The official national checklist of Brazilian plants and fungi, maintained by the Jardim Botânico do Rio de Janeiro. Primary authority for scientific names, family classification, native range, and conservation status of all species.

global_reference_databases.name: iNaturalist — Taxon database
global_reference_databases.description: Global crowdsourced biodiversity observation platform. Used to verify species distribution records in Rio Grande do Sul, confirm presence in Atlantic Forest and Pampa biomes, and source open-access species photography.

global_reference_databases.name: GBIF — Global Biodiversity Information Facility
global_reference_databases.description: International open-access repository of biodiversity occurrence data. Used to cross-check species distribution ranges in southern Brazil and verify Atlantic Forest presence.

global_reference_databases.name: Tropicos — Missouri Botanical Garden
global_reference_databases.description: Botanical nomenclature and specimen database. Used for family-level taxonomy and synonym resolution.

global_reference_databases.name: World Flora Online (WFO)
global_reference_databases.description: Global consensus plant name database. Used as secondary authority for scientific nomenclature.

global_reference_databases.name: Global Wood Density Database (Chave et al. 2009 / Zanne et al. 2009)
global_reference_databases.description: Peer-reviewed global dataset of wood densities (g/cm³) used to calibrate Carbon Sequestration scores. Published in Global Change Biology and Dryad.
global_reference_databases.citation: Zanne AE, et al. (2009). Global wood density database. Dryad. doi:10.5061/dryad.234

global_reference_databases.name: Chave et al. (2014) — Improved allometric models for AGB estimation
global_reference_databases.description: Pan-tropical allometric equations for estimating above-ground biomass from wood density, height and diameter. Foundation for CO₂ absorption estimates.
global_reference_databases.citation: Chave J, et al. (2014). Improved allometric models to estimate the aboveground biomass of tropical trees. Global Change Biology, 20(10), 3177–3190. doi:10.1111/gcb.12629

global_reference_databases.name: REFLORA — Virtual Herbarium Brazil (JBRJ)
global_reference_databases.description: Brazilian herbarium specimen database. Used to verify species morphology descriptions and regional occurrence.

global_reference_databases.name: Lista de Espécies da Fauna Brasileira (ICMBio/MMA)
global_reference_databases.description: Brazilian Red List of threatened species managed by ICMBio. Used to assign conservation status (e.g. Cedrela fissilis as Vulnerable).

global_reference_databases.name: Rede de Sementes do Xingu / Projeto de Restauração da Mata Atlântica (PRMA)
global_reference_databases.description: Brazilian native seed network and Atlantic Forest restoration project documentation. Used for succession role classifications and restoration planting guidelines in southern Brazil.

global_reference_databases.name: Lorenzi, H. — Árvores Brasileiras (Vols. 1–3)
global_reference_databases.description: The definitive illustrated guide to native Brazilian trees, published by Instituto Plantarum. Primary reference for species descriptions, ecology, uses, and distribution in RS.
global_reference_databases.citation: Lorenzi H. (2002–2009). Árvores Brasileiras: Manual de Identificação e Cultivo de Plantas Arbóreas Nativas do Brasil. Vols. 1–3. Instituto Plantarum, Nova Odessa, SP.

global_reference_databases.name: Carvalho, P.E.R. — Espécies Arbóreas Brasileiras (Embrapa)
global_reference_databases.description: Comprehensive Embrapa technical series on Brazilian tree species. Used for growth rate data, timber characteristics and silvicultural notes.
global_reference_databases.citation: Carvalho PER. (2003–2010). Espécies Arbóreas Brasileiras. Vols. 1–4. Embrapa Florestas, Colombo, PR.

global_reference_databases.name: Reis, A. et al. — Restauração de Áreas Degradadas na Mata Atlântica
global_reference_databases.description: Foundational Atlantic Forest restoration manual used to calibrate ecological role scores and succession classifications.
global_reference_databases.citation: Reis A, Bechara FC, Tres DR. (2010). Nucleation in tropical ecological restoration. Scientia Agricola, 67(2), 244–250.

global_reference_databases.name: Kinupp VF & Lorenzi H — Plantas Alimentícias Não Convencionais (PANC) do Brasil
global_reference_databases.description: Comprehensive guide to unconventional food plants of Brazil. Primary reference for Food Security scores and community food use documentation.
global_reference_databases.citation: Kinupp VF, Lorenzi H. (2014). Plantas Alimentícias Não Convencionais (PANC) do Brasil. Instituto Plantarum, Nova Odessa, SP.

global_reference_databases.name: Guarim Neto G & Morais RG — Recursos medicinais de espécies do Cerrado e Mata Atlântica
global_reference_databases.description: Ethnobotanical survey of medicinal plant uses in Brazilian biomes. Used to document medicinal uses relevant to Community Benefit scores.
global_reference_databases.citation: Guarim Neto G, Morais RG. (2003). Recursos medicinais de espécies do Cerrado de Mato Grosso. Acta Botanica Brasilica, 17(4), 561–584.

global_reference_databases.name: Sick, H. — Ornitologia Brasileira
global_reference_databases.description: The authoritative reference on Brazilian birds. Used to document bird-plant interactions for Biodiversity scores.
global_reference_databases.citation: Sick H. (1997). Ornitologia Brasileira. Editora Nova Fronteira, Rio de Janeiro.

global_reference_databases.name: Paise G & Vieira EM — Frugivoria e dispersão de sementes por aves na Mata Atlântica do RS
global_reference_databases.description: Study of frugivory and seed dispersal by birds in the Atlantic Forest of Rio Grande do Sul. Directly relevant to biodiversity scores for fruiting species.
global_reference_databases.citation: Paise G, Vieira EM. (2005). Produção de frutos e a dieta de aves frugívoras do sul do Brasil. Revista Brasileira de Zoologia, 22(3), 751–756.

global_reference_databases.name: Muylaert RL et al. — Ficus (fig trees) as keystone resources in the Neotropics
global_reference_databases.description: Systematic review of fig trees as keystone species in Neotropical ecosystems. Basis for fig species Biodiversity scores of 10.
global_reference_databases.citation: Muylaert RL, et al. (2019). Ficus as a keystone resource in the Neotropics. Biotropica, 51(3), 356–370.

global_reference_databases.name: IBGE — Inventário Florestal Nacional (IFN) — Rio Grande do Sul
global_reference_databases.description: Brazilian National Forest Inventory data for Rio Grande do Sul. Used to calibrate species prevalence and native range within RS.

global_reference_databases.name: Vibrans AC et al. — Inventário Florístico Florestal de Santa Catarina (IFFSC)
global_reference_databases.description: Comprehensive floristic inventory of southern Brazilian Atlantic Forest, directly applicable to adjacent RS species composition.
global_reference_databases.citation: Vibrans AC, et al. (2013). Inventário Florístico Florestal de Santa Catarina. Edifurb, Blumenau, SC.

scoring_framework_references.methodology_note: Bird-plant interaction data from Paise & Vieira (2005) is the primary quantitative source for RS-specific biodiversity scoring. For mammals, Lorenzi (DB11) and broader Atlantic Forest literature are used. Fig trees (Ficus spp.) score 10 based on Muylaert et al. (2019) systematic review of vertebrate-fig interactions.

Kinupp & Lorenzi's PANC Brazil (DB14) is the primary reference for food security scoring. Species listed as having multiple uses, high nutrient content, or active community trade receive 8–10. Species not listed in PANC receive 1–3 unless alternative ethnobotanical documentation is available.

Lorenzi (DB11) and Carvalho/Embrapa (DB12) are the primary references for site-specific RS climate tolerance. Flood tolerance is scored using 2024 Rio Grande do Sul flood recovery literature and Branquilho (Sebastiania commersoniana) is used as the benchmark 10/10 species for complete inundation survival.

Scores derived from composite of wood density (DB06/Zanne et al.), height data (DB12/Carvalho), and lifespan. Allometric equations from Chave et al. 2014 (DB07) applied to estimate CO₂ absorption. Cedrela fissilis and Ficus luschnathiana are benchmark 10/10 species. Important: values are indicative educational estimates, not certified carbon credit measurements.

Succession role (pioneer/secondary/climax) from IFFSC (DB20) and PRMA guidelines (DB10). Irreplaceability scoring follows Reis et al. (DB13) restoration nucleation framework. N-fixing species receive ecological bonus for soil-improvement function beyond their canopy contribution.

Scores integrate food use (DB14/PANC), medicinal use (DB15), timber value (DB12/Carvalho), and Guarani cultural significance where documented. Species with active commercial markets (timber, spice, fruit) receive 8–9. Culturally iconic species with confirmed Guarani use receive 9–10.
